title: Regrouping ordered affine integration in ordinary coordinates
statement:
Fix a finite purity setting $P$ and the actual ordinary-etale integration arrows of [def-sp-nested-affine-formula-data]. Let $B$ be an affine $k$-scheme with finite-type structure morphism $a_B$, let $d,e\ge0$, and let $\mathcal N$ be any etale compact-support normalization for $P.Coefficient$. The equality
$$\operatorname{total}(P,B,a_B,d,e,\mathcal N)=\operatorname{iterated}(P,B,a_B,d,e)$$
holds in the ordinary derived category on $T_d(T_e(B))$. Here total is the rank-$(d+e)$ coefficient-unit integration transpose transported by the specified blockEq and blockProjection, twistPull and etale locality. iterated is the ordered gammaUnit_e pullback followed by gamma_d at $p_e^!A_B$ and the inverse adjunction-normalized exceptional compositor. Both have the same source $A(d+e)[2(d+e)]$ and target $(p_d\,;\,p_e)^!A_B$. The assertion includes $d=0$, $e=0$, both zero, and the empty scheme, and imposes no hypothesis on a non-affine chart or on orientations of general smooth morphisms.

source.place: proof (1), ordered affine integration, chart restriction and normalization

proof.text: For positive ranks, apply affineSpacePurityComposition to the coefficient unit with its canonical ordinary finite-Tor presentation. Identify its total tower and projection by blockEq and blockProjection. The specified affine comparisons are the integration-transposed comparisons, and their exceptional compositor is the conjugate of the same compact-support compositor.

Finite-site comparison carries the ordinary trace, inverse projection map and exceptional adjunction transpose to the displayed pro-etale arrows. Its tensor and pullback comparisons insert exactly source and twistPull. Cancel those isomorphisms and reflect the resulting composition equation by full faithfulness. Normalization is universal, so the equation holds for every N.

If a rank is zero, apply orderedAdjointTower_regrouping at a repeated endpoint. The empty transformation and its adjunction are identities. The source unit comparisons in the affine-space convention and the exceptional identity comparison cancel by the triangles. Both ranks zero gives the same identity. None of these operations assumes a point exists.
